premise: the goal's: unattributed is a gap in the classifier, never a gap in what is knowable. All four rows resolved by replay against the two reference sources. None needed an attribution rule widened.
method: scripts/replay_residue.py on /tmp/sweep_exact.json (39-row current-era sweep). Full branch sets, per the C94 retraction.
note_on_c84: C84 anatomised the THEN-8 unattributed rows using branch_misses and is contaminated by the C94 method error -- its 'engine majority arm carries no damage / empty engine component list' reading (rows 19000093/51,53) is exactly the phantom that method produces. Replay shows those arms are NOT empty of instructions; they are voided by the renderer. C84's crit-arm-absent reading is likewise superseded by C93. C84 needs the same retraction treatment as C92.

19000073/1.boundary: Manectric Thunderbolt into Linoone (maxhp 261), then Linoone Belly Drum
19000073/1.showdown: Thunderbolt -127 leaves 134/261; Belly Drum then costs 130 leaving 4/261 and sets atk to +6
19000073/1.engine_84pct: p1 move=-135 ONLY -- no Belly Drum damage, no boost
19000073/1.cause: the Belly Drum HP GATE is straddled by the damage roll. Showdown moves.ts:1222-1227 refuses when target.hp <= maxhp/2 (130.5); the engine gen3/choice_effects.rs:642-650 refuses when NOT attacker.hp > maxhp/2 (integer 130). The two gates are FAITHFUL to each other on both parities. With the realised roll 127 the survivor is at 134 > gate, so Belly Drum fires. With the engine's collapsed representative roll 135 the survivor is at 126 <= gate, so Belly Drum correctly declines. The engine is RIGHT for the roll it was shown.
19000073/1.why_no_matching_arm: damage collapsing. Without branch_on_damage the engine offers one representative non-crit roll (135) plus crit arms (253, capped_lethal 261); the realised 127 is not among them, so no arm can carry the Belly Drum consequence.

disposition.detail: the same shape as the registered limit:roll_divergent_lethality, with the threshold being Belly Drum's maxhp/2 gate rather than 0 HP. A branch set against a single realised sample: the methodology cannot settle it while the realised roll is absent from the support.
disposition.caveat: this is a limit only because damage is collapsed. It is not a statement that the engine is wrong -- it is demonstrably right. If branch_on_damage were extended to roll-gated self-damage effects the row would resolve, so the limit is a property of the instrument's resolution, not of the engine.

19000093/51.boundary: Rayquaza Rock Slide into Seaking; Seaking Hydro Pump into Rayquaza; rain upkeep; Seaking Leftovers
19000093/51.engine: the three largest arms (44.30%, 25.31%, 11.81% -- over 85% of the mass) carry NO components at all and are marked LOSSY=['segmentation_failed']. Only 10% of the mass is usable.
19000093/51.cause: NOT an engine error. The underlying instruction list of the majority arm is correct and complete: Damage SideTwo 94, DecrementPP SideTwo M2, Damage SideOne 63, DecrementWeatherTurnsRemaining, Heal SideTwo 18 -- both hits present, in Showdown's order. The RENDERER voids it. rust/pokezero-search/src/events.rs:766-779: when segment() returns None the branch is returned with zero components. segment() (events.rs:416+) searches for a first-mover instruction prefix with a consistent second-mover continuation and yields None when no split is consistent; on this boundary none is.
19000093/51.not_isolated: the specific predicate inside segment() that rejects every split here is NOT yet pinned. Candidate worth checking first: the first mover's DecrementPP is absent from the list while the second mover's is present, so a PP-marker-delimited split has nothing to anchor the first segment on.

disposition.detail: segment() must not void a branch whose instruction list is well-formed. Failing that, the matcher must not treat a segmentation_failed branch as a usable arm carrying zero components -- silently reading 'no components' off a branch that was never rendered is the same reading error C94 retracted, promoted into the instrument.

19000093/53.boundary: Rayquaza Dragon Dance; Seaking Megahorn into Rayquaza (resisted); rain ends; Seaking Leftovers
19000093/53.cause: a LABELLING error, not a numeric one. Raw instructions are Boost SideOne Attack 1, Boost SideOne Speed 1, Damage SideOne 55, DecrementWeatherTurnsRemaining, ChangeWeather RAIN->NONE, Heal SideTwo 18 -- Megahorn's damage in exactly Showdown's position. But no move marker (DecrementPP / SetLastUsedMove for SideTwo) precedes it, so the segmenter files it in the RESIDUAL segment. residual is an EXACT-bucket component, so the legal roll difference 55 vs 53 is compared for equality and rejected. In the move bucket the same pair matches under ordinary roll tolerance.
19000093/53.contrast: 19000093/51 above DOES carry DecrementPP SideTwo for the second mover. The marker is emitted inconsistently between the two boundaries, which is the thing to fix.

disposition.detail: emit the second mover's move marker consistently so its damage lands in the move segment. A move's damage must never be bucketed as a residual -- that silently converts a roll-tolerant comparison into an exact one.

19000152/53.boundary: p1 switches to Armaldo; Espeon Hidden Power into Armaldo; Espeon Leftovers; Espeon perish count reaches 0 and it faints
19000152/53.showdown: |-heal|p2a: Espeon|132/224|[from] item: Leftovers, then |-start|p2a: Espeon|perish0, |upkeep|, |faint|p2a: Espeon -- the faint carries NO -damage line
19000152/53.cause: a representation difference about how a non-damaging faint is expressed. Perish Song kills by setting HP to 0 with no damage message, so Showdown's component set has nothing for it. The engine renders the same state change as capped_lethal=-132 (Espeon's full HP after its Leftovers tick), which the matcher counts as an extra engine component with no observed counterpart. Both descriptions of the end state are identical; only the event vocabulary differs.
19000152/53.roll_note: p1's -118 vs -111 is an ordinary Hidden Power roll difference inside the window and is not what rejects this row.

disposition.detail: a |faint| with no preceding |-damage| must reconcile against an engine capped_lethal equal to the victim's remaining HP. Either the renderer should not emit a damage component for a perish/curse-class faint, or the matcher should recognise the pairing. This is decidable from both sources and is NOT a comparison limit.

tally.comment: three of the four are instrument defects and one is a genuine limit. NOT ONE of the four required an attribution rule to be widened, and in none of them is the gen3 engine's simulation wrong.

bonus_finding_for_c95_I5: C95 left I5 hedged between engine and harness. events.rs:751-765 settles it: the renderer already special-cases replacement plies, but only for (switch, none) shapes -- 'Replacement / pivot plies ((switch, none) shapes): no end-of-turn phase'. I5's boundary is (switch, SWITCH), which that predicate does not cover, so end_of_turn_triggered returns true and Leftovers is applied on a turn Showdown never ran. The fix is to extend the existing replacement predicate to the double-switch shape, in the renderer.
